source: Edward Henning, Kalacakra and the Tibetan Calendar (2007), Chapter VI Different Calculation Systems
scope: printed pp296–343 / PDF pp316–363 selected full-text passages

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning presents a karaṇa epoch of Monday 23 March 806, Julian day 2015531, for the original Kālacakra computation as distinct from later Tibetan siddhānta epoch policies.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: The karaṇa mean synodic month is 29.5305556 solar days, whereas the Tibetan siddhānta model used in Chapter I takes 29.5305870; Henning distinguishes rate error from epoch position error.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning derives a karaṇa year length of 365.258516 solar days and compares it to a siddhānta figure of 365.270645, noting separate modern sidereal/tropical reference values.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: In analysing planetary calculations Henning proposes that a Venus epoch instruction to subtract 84 may reflect a scribal error for add 84; he explicitly presents this as his conjecture, not an established source correction.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning demonstrates the Phugpa mean-weekday relation that 39,592 lunar months equal 175,682 weeks; equivalently, their weekday advance of 60,599 days corresponds to 8,657 complete seven-day cycles after removing four-week components.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: The Phugpa mean solar-longitude calculation uses a 65-solar-year/804-lunar-month commensurability and a worked month remainders chain deriving 22;44,6,1,41.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning reports scant surviving documentation for the Tsurphu tradition’s formation, including a lost Great Text on Astronomy; inferred historical reasoning must not be presented as the extant author's exact observations.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: In Henning's reconstruction Phugpa employs a theoretical winter-solstice offset of 23 degrees, Tsurphu 14 degrees; he notes mean solar-longitude outputs differ by less than the naively expected nine degrees.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning infers, from retrospective calculation and absent direct observation records, that Tsurphu solstice observations may have been about one day late; this is an analyst's reconstruction, not independently documented historical practice.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Karma Ngelek Tendzin's Tsurphu calculation epoch is Wednesday 26 March 1732 (JD 2353745), including distinct mean weekday and mean Sun fractional constants.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Jamgon Kongtrul's separate Tsurphu epoch is Monday 19 April 1852 (JD 2397598), preserving the same mean-motion constants but using new epoch offsets.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning calculates mean new-moon timing for 1447 with Phugpa about 8.3 nadi before modern calculation and Tsurphu about 5.5 nadi before; the comparison concerns mean positions, not actual human predictions.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: When the intercalation index is zero at new moon Phugpa/Error Correction places mean Sun at the beginning of a zodiac sign, but Tsurphu at longitude 0;29,34,5,37 lunar-mansion units, approximately 6.574 decimal degrees Aries, not 0 degrees.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning gives the Tsurphu monthly definition-point window as 0;29,78 to 0;31,80 in its notation, about 6.574 to 7.022 decimal zodiac degrees, contrasting it with a theoretical point near 16 degrees for a 14-degree solstice shift.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_notes.paraphrase: Henning describes an independently developed Sherab Ling calendar with epoch Sunday 29 March 1987 (JD 2446884) and a solar mean-motion adjustment closer to the Kālacakra karaṇa rather than the standard Phugpa/Tsurphu figures; treat as additional competing tradition.
source_notes.status: author's original mathematical study of traditional Sanskrit/Tibetan source methods; historical claims and author conjectures separated

source_risk_notes: Henning's 84 Venus correction is explicitly conjectural, not an established literal source reading.
Historical Tsurphu solstice observations are reconstructed without direct surviving records.
6.574 in intercalation description means decimal degrees; source sexagesimal mansion coordinates are the primary precise datum.
Numerical agreement with astronomical rates is not evidence of astrological life-event prediction.
